about: Everyday prompts for scripts/evals/artifact-routing.mts. expect "artifacts": the agent should save to artifacts.space. expect "elsewhere": a near miss that belongs in chat or in the repository, so saving an artifact is a false positive.

cases.prompt: Write up the plan for moving our cron jobs from Heroku Scheduler to GitHub Actions: list the six jobs, port them one at a time behind a flag, then turn off Heroku.
Make a report for the team on last week's incidents: two API outages (Tuesday 14 minutes, Thursday 9 minutes, both from connection pool exhaustion) and one failed deploy that we rolled back.
Save this for later: we chose Postgres advisory locks over Redis locks for the migration runner, because we already run Postgres and need no new infrastructure.
Draft a spec for a rate limiter on the public API: per-token and per-IP limits, a 429 with Retry-After, and limits set per plan.
Take notes on this standup so the team can read them later: Ana finished the billing export, Raj is blocked on the SSO certificate, and we ship the beta on Friday.
Write a decision record: we are moving the web app from Webpack to Turbopack because builds are four times faster. The risk is two plugins we must replace.
Write a runbook for rotating the Stripe webhook secret without downtime.
I'm signing off. Write a handoff for whoever picks up the search reindex tomorrow: the backfill is 60% done, the job can resume where it stopped, and the alias swap is the last step.
Compare Resend, Postmark, and Amazon SES for our transactional email, and write it up so I can share it with the team.
Keep this checklist somewhere I can find it next week: renew the TLS certificate, rotate the deploy key, and archive the old S3 bucket.
Publish a page that explains our on-call rotation and escalation steps for new hires.
Write a doc for the team that describes the three webhooks we send (invoice.paid, invoice.failed, customer.deleted) and their payloads.
Write the postmortem for yesterday's outage: a bad config push turned off the cache, p95 latency reached 4 seconds for 22 minutes, and we rolled back.
Draft a one-page product brief for team workspaces: shared projects, roles, and an activity feed.
Summarize what we decided about the pricing tiers and share it with the team: Free, Pro at $12, and Team at $20 per seat.
Make a status page for the launch: 5 tasks done, 3 in progress, and 1 blocked on App Store review.
Write an onboarding guide for new engineers: clone the repo, run pnpm install, copy .env.example, run pnpm dev, and where to ask for help.
We just worked out how the retry queue should work: exponential backoff from 1 second to 5 minutes, at most 8 tries, then a dead-letter table. Write it up.
Write release notes for version 2.3 that I can send to customers: dark mode, CSV export, and faster search.
Put together a Q1 roadmap doc for the platform team: observability, cost cuts, and the Node 26 upgrade.
Save my research notes on SQLite versus Postgres for the desktop app so I can come back to them: SQLite needs no server and syncs as a file; Postgres gives us one schema with the web app.
What's the difference between a mutex and a semaphore? One paragraph.
Fix the typo in README.md: "recieve" should be "receive".
Add a unit test for the add function in src/math.ts.
Explain what this error means: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map').
Add a section to this repo's README that explains how to run it locally.
Rename the add function in src/math.ts to sum.
Write a commit message for a change that adds retries to the webhook sender.
In one line, what does package.json say this project is?
